extracted.intended_audience: applicants and institutional staff using ASSIST/eRA Commons to prepare and submit NIH (and related HHS/SAMHSA) grant applications, including human subjects and clinical trials data
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step procedural and form-content guidance for completing ASSIST application forms, with particular emphasis on the PHS Human Subjects & Clinical Trials Information form, Inclusion Enrollment Reports, participant-level data rules, ClinicalTrials.gov export/upload, and several non-research form requirements (SF-424 family, project abstract, budget narrative, biosketches).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required field entry to save forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Data elements marked with an asterisk (*) are required to save the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to enter required data before starting. Validation warnings will prevent saving if required fields are missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use application form instructions for field-level guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: For field-level instructions on each question, consult the application form instructions (HTML or PDF) at the How to Apply/Application Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Application Guide for substantive content directions; ASSIST provides UI but field content guidance comes from the Application Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form edit reservation and locking behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Selecting the Edit button reserves the form, enables it for editing, and prevents others from editing it simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edit must be selected to open fields for editing. While reserved, others cannot edit the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form expand/collapse behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms with grouped sections are expanded by default (Expand All checked); individual fields can be expanded/collapsed using the arrow on the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unselect Expand All to collapse groups; use the field arrow for per-field expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save options semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: There are multiple save actions: Save and Keep Lock, Save and Release Lock, Save and Add (multi-page forms), and Cancel and Release Lock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Save and Keep Lock saves and keeps form locked for further editing; Save and Release Lock saves and allows others to edit; Save and Add saves current page and opens next (not on all forms); Cancel and Release Lock returns to read-only and does not save changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning when navigating with unsaved data
rubrics_metrics.description: If unsaved data exists when navigating between tabs, ASSIST displays a warning: 'Exiting without saving will result in losing the data entered. Do you wish to save before exiting?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: Go Back to save, choose a save option, or Continue to move without saving. Return to the form to save if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Session timeout behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: ASSIST employs a session time-out feature that logs you out after inactivity; it displays a warning indicating remaining time until automatic logout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To prevent automatic time-out, select Continue Working from the warning screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study records must be added only once per application
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies must only be added once for each application regardless of how many times they are used by other cores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multi-component applications that share protocols, include the study in the Overall and reference it in other cores using the designated box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delayed Onset Study rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A Delayed Onset Study (marked as an anticipated clinical trial) can fulfill NOFO requirements and requires a Justification explaining why the study cannot be described at submission time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple delayed-onset studies may be grouped in a single record. You cannot add a regular or delayed study if you answered 'No' to the human subjects question in the R&R Other Project Information form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Record section structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Study Record consists of named sections: Section 1 Basic Information; Section 2 Study Population Characteristics; Section 3 Protection and Monitoring Plans; Section 4 Protocol Synopsis; Section 5 Other Clinical Trial-related Attachments; Section 6 Clinical Milestone Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section applicability varies (e.g., Section 4 & 5 appear for clinical trials; Section 6 appears in post-submission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 1 — Basic Information requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1 includes a Study Title (up to 600 characters, unique to your organization), an exemption question (required/system enforced), exemption code information at the study level, a clinical trial questionnaire, and an optional ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier (NCT number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all four clinical trial questionnaire items are answered Yes, the study is considered a clinical trial and Section 5 will appear. Enter NCT in specified format and use Populate to import CT.gov data (then verify completeness).

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Project Exemptions summary (1, 2, 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Exemptions applicable to NIH are Exemption 1 (educational settings with normal practices), Exemption 2 (education tests, surveys, interviews, or public behavior observations unless identifiable/risky), and Exemption 4 (secondary research using identifiable information/biospecimens if publicly available or recorded so subjects cannot be re-identified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to NIH infographic for details and limits, especially regarding children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 2 — Study Population Characteristics and conditions limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 2 captures conditions and eligibility criteria and demographics; required for all human subject studies unless exemption 4 applies. Use Add New Condition to enter up to 20 conditions or areas of focus, each limited to 255 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first few answers in R&R Other Project Information populate the first three questions here. Section 2 includes the Inclusion Enrollment Report (IER) intake form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion Enrollment Report (IER) content & uniqueness
rubrics_metrics.description: IERs (up to 20 per Study Record) must indicate whether an existing dataset/resource will be used and whether enrollment location type is domestic or foreign. The Inclusion Enrollment Report Title should be unique to help identify the report; human subjects study title appears by default but can be changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IER includes Planned and Cumulative enrollment tables; planned counts must be updated online; cumulative counts can be edited online or via participant-level data upload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing Cumulative (Actual) Inclusion counts — two methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Cumulative (Actual) inclusion counts can be updated either by editing cells online in the web form or by uploading participant-level data using the Upload Participant Level Data Attachment button.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uploading participant-level data is required for some applications. Use provided CSV template; altering column headers or format will cause upload errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant-level data template restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: When uploading participant-level data, you must use the provided CSV template and must not alter the columns or category titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data may be copied into the template from other sources. After saving the template file, use Upload Participant Level Data Attachment to update cumulative counts. You can download current participant-level data for records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress-report participant-level data requirement (effective date)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual-level participant data on sex, race, ethnicity and age at enrollment are required in progress reports for competitive applications submitted for due dates on or after January 25, 2019 (NIH Guide Notice NOT-OD-18-116).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure participant-level data collection and template use satisfy this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant-level data fields and allowed values
rubrics_metrics.description: Participant-level data entries include Race, Ethnicity, Sex, Age, and Age Unit. Race/Ethnicity/Sex must contain valid values per OMB standards (consistent with Grants.gov form).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Race values: American Indian, Asian, Hawaiian, Black, White, More than one race, Unknown. Ethnic values: Not Hispanic or Latino, Hispanic or Latino, Unknown. Sex values: Male, Female, Unknown. Age must be a whole number 0–9999. Age unit values: Minutes, Hours, Days, Weeks, Months, Years, Ninety Plus, Unknown. If Age Unit is not Ninety Plus or Unknown, an Age number is required; if Ninety Plus or Unknown, Age must be blank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 3 — Protection of Human Subjects attachment
rubrics_metrics.description: All human subjects studies must provide a Protection of Human Subjects attachment and answer multi-site questions as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposing a multi-site study that uses the same protocol at more than one domestic site for non-exempt research, attach a plan describing compliance with NIH single-IRB policy. Note: the IRB Plan attachment is not required for Forms F version 2.0 and later. Other items in this section (Data and Safety Monitoring Plan, DSMB question, Overall Structure of Study Team) generally apply only to clinical trials, though others can include them if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 4 — Protocol Synopsis requirements for independent clinical trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 4 (protocol synopsis) is required only for study records involving independent clinical trials and includes multiple required fields and attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required items include: Narrative Study Description (up to 32,000 characters); Primary Purpose dropdown; up to 20 Interventions (type, name, description); Study Phase selection with NIH-defined Phase III identification; Intervention Model; Masking Information (if 'Yes', at least one related box must be checked); Allocation; 1–50 Outcome Measures (Name and Time Frame limit 255 chars; Brief Description limit 999 chars); Statistical Design and Power attachment; Subject Participation Duration attachment (255 char limit); Question 4.6 about FDAAA applicability; Dissemination Plan attachment (usually one per application; may be attached in multiple studies). Many fields map directly to ClinicalTrials.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 5 — Other clinical trial-related attachments appearance condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 5 appears only for clinical trial study records and only when an attachment is specifically requested in the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 5 is triggered when questions 1.4.a through 1.4.d are all Yes (study indicates a clinical trial). If attachments are required, follow NOFO directions and contact program staff listed in the NOFO if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 6 — Clinical Milestone Plan (post-submission only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 6 appears only in post-submission forms (HSCT Post Submission) to record milestone dates and whether the study is an applicable clinical trial under FDAAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Question 6.6 addresses FDAAA applicability. Use the 'Identifying an Applicable Clinical Trial under FDAAA' flowchart for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exporting or uploading Human Subjects data to ClinicalTrials.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: ASSIST provides options to export study data to an XML file or upload directly to ClinicalTrials.gov (via PRS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To upload directly, the sponsoring organization must have a Protocol Registration and Results System (PRS) account. The Export XML button appears only for study records that propose a clinical trial (yes to 1.4a–1.4d). If uploading directly, check Upload box (only appears for studies with a study ID but without an NCT and not previously uploaded), enter Organization Name (one-word PRS org name) and Unique Protocol ID (up to 30 characters), then enter PRS username/password and click Upload. Successful upload message instructs logging into PRS to complete registration; unsuccessful upload may be due to an existing NCT or previous upload — in that case use PRS to update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export XML file requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Exporting to XML creates a local file containing the study's Human Subjects Study data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Export XML is available only for clinical trial studies (yes to 1.4a–1.4d). Organization Name is the PRS one-word org name; Unique Protocol ID can be any unique identifier up to 30 characters. Save the XML to your computer's default download folder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upload XML file to ClinicalTrials.gov via PRS
rubrics_metrics.description: A signing official can upload an XML file with HSS data into ClinicalTrials.gov PRS to populate corresponding fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRS account is required. After logging into PRS, select Upload Record XML and upload the file. PRS will show warnings for additional required information because HSS is only a subset of PRS required fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF-424 (Application for Federal Assistance) for non-research grants
rubrics_metrics.description: SF-424 must be completed by applicants for all non-research grants; it is part of the application package and is accessed from the NOFO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NOFO instructions to include the SF-424 as required. Use Grants.gov application kit and referenced instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF-424A budget form completion guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: SF424-A (Budget Information – Non-Construction Programs) is designed for funds from one or more grant programs; fill out Sections B, C, and E of the SF-424A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is highly recommended to use the sample budget format in Appendix J to expedite review. Adhere to any existing federal grantor agency guidelines prescribing how budgeted amounts should be shown for different functions/activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF-424-B, -C, -D instructions and sources
rubrics_metrics.description: SF424-B (Assurances for Non-Construction), SF424-C (Budget Information for Construction Programs), and SF424-D (Assurances for Construction Programs) each have specific instructions and agency sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read and follow the guidance links provided (How to Apply Application Guide and form instruction PDFs). SF424-B requires reading assurances on SAMHSA website and checking 'I Agree' if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Abstract Summary length and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Abstract must not be longer than 30 lines and should include project name, population(s) to be served (demographics and clinical characteristics), strategies/interventions, project goals and measurable objectives, including number of people to be served annually and throughout the lifetime of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the first five lines or less of the abstract, write a summary that can be used in publications, reports to Congress, or press releases if funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Narrative required detail and components
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must include a detailed Budget Narrative in addition to the Budget Form SF-424A and explain how each budgeted amount was determined to assess allowability, allocability, and reasonableness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specifics: Personnel (roles/responsibilities), Fringe Benefits (list components of rate), Travel (airfare, number staff, lodging, days, per diem, mileage), Supplies (describe need if not obvious), Contractual (explain need and relation to project), Other (list each category).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project/Performance Site Location purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect location information on the site(s) where work funded under this grant will be performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete site location details as required by the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative content requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must address how the applicant will implement and meet the goals and objectives of the program; attach the project narrative file (PDF) inside the Project Narrative Attachment Form per NOFO Part I guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the NOFO for specific content and formatting instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF-LLL (Disclosure of Lobbying Activities) legal requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal law prohibits use of appropriated funds for publicity/propaganda supporting or defeating legislation; sign and submit SF-LLL if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete SF-LLL when lobbying activities disclosure is required by the NOFO or law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other narrative attachments as specified by NOFO
rubrics_metrics.description: The NOFO will specify if additional forms available on SAMHSA's website are required; additional forms may be required for the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the NOFO and SAMHSA resources for any program-specific attachments (e.g., participant protection forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch content items
rubrics_metrics.description: Biographical sketches should include name, educational background (schools, locations, dates, degrees, major field), professional experience, honors with dates, recent relevant publications, and other sources of support (all funds/resources available to key personnel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing CVs may be used if updated and containing all requested items; for new biosketches include the listed items in the most suitable format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Job description required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Job descriptions should include title of position, description of duties/responsibilities, qualifications, supervisory relationships, skills/knowledge required, personal qualities, amount of travel/special conditions, salary range, and hours per day or week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete job descriptions consistent with the positions proposed in the budget and personnel sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and Participant Protection narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: In Section F of the application, describe procedures relating to Confidentiality, Participant Protection, and the Protection of Human Subjects Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address how participant data confidentiality will be maintained and how human subjects protections comply with regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS 690 form requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Every grant applicant must have a completed HHS 690 form on file with the Department of Health and Human Services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure HHS 690 is completed and on file as part of application administrative requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charitable Choice Form SMA 170 applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The SMA 170 form (Assurance of Compliance with SAMHSA Charitable Choice Statutes and Regulations) is required only for programs offering substance abuse prevention or treatment services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delete if not applicable; if applicable, complete the SMA 170 as part of the application package.
